## Why visit

A particularly strong new reason to consider a north-coast beer excursion. Liverpool CAMRA named this convivial, book-lined former restaurant its Pub of the Year in both 2025 and 2026. A candlelit conservatory, five changing casks and a documented cider offer make it an inviting tasting-and-conversation stop rather than a generic suburban bar. Pair with the nearby Corner Post or Waterloo’s Volunteer Canteen/Four Ashes, allowing time for the rail and street connections.

## Beer

Five changing cask ales from independent breweries; the choice rotates and is not guaranteed until checked on the day. CAMRA names Black Lodge, Salopian and Thornbridge as changing cask suppliers; no individual beer is fixed.

## Cider and perry

**Real cider documented; reconfirm stock.** CAMRA flags real cider and normally describes two boxed ciders, often Seacider; verify the exact product, as flavours and production methods differ.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Plan the visit

Typically afternoon/evening opening and earlier closure than the city's late pubs. The current listing says wheelchair access through the conservatory by portable ramp; confirm if needed.

**Getting there:** Blundellsands & Crosby railway station is around a walk away; combine with nearby Crosby pubs rather than an assumed Liverpool centre stroll.
